Seminar Title:

Investigation on the Mechanical and Wear behavior of Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) 3D printed parts

Seminar Type:

Department:

Mechanical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Kiran Suna ( Rollno : 523me1006)

Student

Date and Time:

Contact:

Sandhyarani Biswas

Abstract:

Additive manufacturing (AM) (also called as 3D printing) is a process that builds layers to make a physical part from a digital model. In contrast to subtractive manufacturing, 3D objects are manufactured by successively depositing material in layers. It offers many advantages, including material flexibility, design freedom, reduction in material waste, and an increased range of complex structures. Unlike traditional processes, AM requires no tooling and dies to fabricate parts, reducing material waste and labour costs. Apart from the above advantages, this method mainly comes under the green manufacturing process as the scrap and noise pollution are significantly reduced in their usage. This technology has many potential applications in aerospace, automotive, biomedical, consumer products, etc. Pure polymer structures produced via AM techniques attain poor mechanical strength and stiffness due to the inherent weak mechanical properties of raw polymers. Attempts have been made by researchers to overcome the poor mechanical performance of such printed parts. AM of polymer matrix composites with enhanced mechanical properties have resolved these limitations by introducing the reinforcements to polymer, such reinforcements include fibers or nanomaterials, forming a fiber-reinforced polymer composites, which are considered as high performance materials due to their exceptional functionality. Fused deposition modelling (FDM) method has been extensively used to manufacture 3D printed parts and PLA is one of the most commonly used materials in the form of filament in FDM method. The objective of the present work is to investigate the mechanical and wear properties of the polylactic acid (PLA) and carbon fiber reinforced polylactic acid (CF-PLA) fabricated by FDM process. The experiments are conducted based on Taguchi's L27 orthogonal array design. The process parameters like the layer thickness, infill density, printing speed, raster angle and line width are considered for optimization. Taguchi design and grey relational analysis (GRA) are employed for multi-response optimization to optimizing the mechanical properties. The analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to investigate the percentage of contribution by each parameter. Finally, SEM analysis of the composite fracture surface was conducted to reveal the microscopic failure mechanisms.
